You can find visiting information and book a visit on the Askham Grange Prison main page.

Our commitment to you

Supporting family relationships at HMP Askham Grange

We are committed to helping women in our care stay connected with the people who matter most to them.

When we refer to families in this document, we mean a wide range of important relationships. This includes relatives, legal guardians, partners, close friends, or any significant person identified by the prisoner as their next of kin.

For care leavers, this may also include someone who provides statutory support services.

Research has shown that positive family relationships can play an important role in reducing reoffending and helping people successfully rebuild their lives after prison.

In 2017, a review by Lord Farmer highlighted the importance of maintaining family ties during imprisonment.

In 2019, a second review focused specifically on the needs of women in prison and their families (PDF).

HMP Askham Grange has worked to put the recommendations from these reviews into practice.

We also consider recommendations from organisations such as HM Inspectorate of Prisons (HMIP), the Independent Monitoring Board (IMB), and the Measuring the Quality of Prison Life (MQPL) survey to ensure we continue to improve our support for women and their families.

Why is this important?

We recognise that imprisonment affects not only the individual in prison but also the people who care about them.

Family members and loved ones may worry about the person in prison and may be unsure how best to support them. They may need help understanding how to:

support someone through their sentence

maintain relationships with children, siblings, and other family members

encourage recovery from substance misuse issues

support mental and physical health needs

prepare for release and reintegration into family and community life

We know that families can play a vital role in helping people make positive changes and lead crime-free lives after release.

At the same time, we understand that not all family relationships are positive.

In some cases, family members may have been directly or indirectly affected by a person’s offending behaviour, including domestic abuse or issues related to substance misuse.

These situations can place significant strain on relationships and may cause lasting harm.

For this reason, we aim to provide support that recognises the needs and experiences of both prisoners and their families.

Our approach

HMP Askham Grange has a multi-agency family team that meets every week to review and improve the support available to women and their families.

By working together with partner organisations, we aim to ensure that our services are responsive, effective, and focused on the needs of those we support.

Support and services offered

What we offer

We provide a range of services and support to help women maintain relationships with their families, prepare for release, and access the support they need while in our care.

Family information booklet

When someone arrives at Askham Grange, they can choose to have a family information booklet sent to their next of kin or a significant person in their life.

The booklet explains:

how the prison operates

the support services available

how families can raise concerns

how families can support their loved one while they are in prison

Letters

There is no limit to the number of letters a prisoner can receive.

Women are encouraged to keep in touch with family and friends through letter writing. Each prisoner can apply for:

One free letter each week

Additional free letters if they have children under 18

Free letters may also be provided for important matters such as:

housing

employment

legal issues

Writing materials can be purchased through weekly canteen or from the prison shop.

Education classes are available for anyone who would like to improve their reading and writing skills.

Release on temporary licence (ROTL)

Release on temporary licence (ROTL) allows eligible prisoners to leave the prison for approved purposes, including maintaining family relationships and preparing for resettlement.

ROTL may include:

childcare resettlement leave

day release

overnight release

special purpose licences

Applications are assessed individually and are subject to eligibility criteria and risk assessments.

Women can apply through their prison offender manager (POM).

During ROTL, prisoners are expected to make good use of their time by taking part in activities that support family relationships and successful resettlement.

Our Offender Management Unit works closely with community-based offender managers when assessing applications.

Family days

Family days let women to spend quality time with their families in a welcoming and supportive environment.

Activities may include:

family games and activities

time to relax together

shared meals

We hold special themed family days during school holidays.

These are a fantastic opportunity for families to spend quality time together. They are packed with fun games, interactive activities, and child-friendly entertainment. These events encourage families to connect, laugh, and create lasting memories.

We also host adults-only family events. These offer a variety of engaging activities alongside the chance to meet and speak with staff from different departments who work closely with prisoners.

Both events include a great selection of food, helping to make the day enjoyable, welcoming, and memorable for everyone involved.

Prisoners can apply to attend these events. They are consistently well received by families.

Visits hall

The visits hall is a large, welcoming space where women can spend time with family and friends.

Children are encouraged to interact and play with their family member during visits.

Our facilities include:

a soft play area

board games

activity bags available from the tea bar
